summary: One more article in myseliasan's built-in manual, in all four shipped languages (4 files), taking it to 22 articles per language: "Working inside a node" (Fleet section), documenting the embedded node pages opened by the Manage action -- what each kind of node (camera recorder, sensor hub, door controller) exposes, that the browser never talks to the node directly (everything rides the control channel the node dialled outward), live video's WebRTC-then-snapshot-fallback behaviour, and the one property support tends to get asked about: your permission to REACH a node's pages comes from this control plane, but your permission to DO things there is evaluated by the node itself against your node-access grant, so a refusal inside these pages did not come from here. Also documents that an empty page there can mean the node is unreachable rather than genuinely empty, what the remote console escape hatch does and does not tunnel (no streaming endpoints), and the ordered troubleshooting checklist for when a node's pages will not load. Cross-links to "Users, roles and access"'s node-access section.
compatibility: Backward compatible, additive only. Content only -- no code, config, schema or route changes; the article is markdown compiled into the binary by the existing //go:embed and served by the manual endpoints that already exist. Not referenced by any HelpButton/TAB_HELP/SETUP_STEP_HELP contextual-help target, so the frontend drift guard's target count is unaffected; it is reached only through the manual's own table of contents and search; the article itself cross-links out to "Users, roles and access"'s node-access section. Anchors are identical across all four languages and the article resolves in the manual conformance suite (metadata, language parity, links, anchors).
